items.q: Why does my basement only flood in heavy rain?
items.preview: Groundwater rises or the sewer fills. The cause decides the fix.

items.q: Does insurance cover a flooded basement?

items.q: What's the difference between a sump pump and an ejector pump?
items.preview: A sump pump removes groundwater. An ejector pump moves basement wastewater to the sewer.
items.answer: A [sump pump](/naperville/sump-pumps) removes groundwater from a pit and sends it outside. An [ejector pump](/naperville/ejector-pump) lifts wastewater from a basement bathroom or laundry up to the sewer line.

blocks.h2: What Does a Catch Basin Do?
blocks.body: A catch basin is a buried box with a grate at a low point in the yard or driveway. Runoff flows in, sand, mulch and leaves settle at the bottom, and water leaves through an outlet pipe. When the bottom fills, the outlet clogs and water stays in the yard. We clean basins, clear outlet pipes and repair basins that have cracked or shifted.

items.q: Do I have to keep my catch basin clear in Naperville?

items.q: Can a clogged catch basin flood my basement?

items.q: Is a catch basin the same as a French drain?
items.preview: No. A catch basin collects surface water at one low spot. A French drain is a gravel trench.
items.answer: No. A catch basin collects surface water at a low point and sends it out through a pipe. A French drain is a gravel-filled trench with a perforated pipe that collects water along its length. We clean and repair catch basins and their outlet pipes.

blocks.h2: What Does an Ejector Pump Do?
blocks.body: Plumbing in a basement usually sits below the sewer line that leaves the house, so it can't drain by gravity. Its drains run to a sealed basin instead. When the basin fills, a float switches on the ejector pump, which pushes the wastewater up into the main sewer line. It's not the same as a [sump pump](/naperville/sump-pumps), which only handles groundwater.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber working on the discharge pipe of a basement sump pump

blocks.h2: Signs Your Ejector Pump Is Failing
blocks.intro: Watch for:

tiles.body: Many basins have a high-water alarm. If it's sounding, stop using basement fixtures and call before the basin overflows.
A sealed basin shouldn't smell. Odor points to a failed lid seal, a vent problem or a basin that isn't emptying.
If the basement toilet or shower backs up while upstairs drains work fine, the ejector pump is the first suspect.
A pump that never shuts off is fighting a stuck float, a failed check valve or a worn motor.

blocks.h2: Ejector Pumps in Naperville Homes
blocks.intro: Naperville's boom-era homes often came with finished basements, and finished basements often come with bathrooms.

items.body: If your basement was finished 15 to 25 years ago, the pump serving it may be original. Many have never been serviced.
In homes with an [overhead sewer system](/naperville/overhead-sewer-systems), every basement drain flows to the ejector pit.
The city warns that wipes plug pumps, and it's true at home too. Only toilet paper belongs in a basement toilet.
The check valve above the pump keeps wastewater from falling back into the basin. When it fails, the pump runs more and wears out faster. We check it on every call.

blocks.h2: What Is Hydro Jetting?
blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

The floor drain, basement bathroom and laundry are rerouted to a sealed pit. An [ejector pump](/naperville/ejector-pump) pushes the wastewater up to a pipe near the ceiling, and a check valve keeps it from falling back. Gravity takes it from there.

Snowmelt and spring rain raise the water table around Naperville basements. That's when pumps run the most, and when an old one is most likely to quit.

items.q: Where should my sump pump drain in Naperville?
items.preview: Outside, away from the house. Not into the sanitary sewer.
items.answer: Outside, away from the foundation. The City of Naperville says sump pumps shouldn't discharge into the sanitary sewer. If yours does, it adds water to the sewer during storms, and we can reroute it.

items.q: Do I need a battery backup sump pump?
items.preview: If your basement is finished, yes.
items.answer: If you have a finished basement or anything valuable down there, yes. The storms that fill the pit fastest can also cut the power.

items.q: How long does a sump pump last?

items.q: Will a sump pump stop sewer backups?
items.preview: No. It handles groundwater. Sewer backups need a different fix.
items.answer: No. A sump pump moves groundwater. Water coming up through a floor drain is a sewer problem and needs clearing, a backflow valve or an [overhead sewer system](/naperville/overhead-sewer-systems).

blocks.h2: How a Tankless Water Heater Works
blocks.body: A tankless heater warms water only when a hot tap is open. Cold water passes through a heat exchanger, a burner or element heats it on the spot and it flows to the faucet or shower. Since there's no tank, it doesn't run out. It does have a limit on how much hot water it can make at once, so sizing matters, and it needs the right gas line, venting or electrical service.

blocks.h2: What Is Trenchless Sewer Repair?
blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers setting up sewer camera and cable equipment beside a home's foundation before a trenchless sewer repair

blocks.h2: Why Trenchless Fits Naperville Homes
blocks.intro: Naperville homeowners maintain the sewer line from the house to the main, and many have invested years in their yards. Lining protects both.

items.body: Roots are Naperville's number one cause of backups. A liner seals every joint and crack in the section it covers, so roots have nowhere left to get in.
A trench cuts through the root zone of the trees you want to keep. Lining works inside the pipe.
In older neighborhoods near downtown, clay laterals with cracked joints are what lining handles best.

items.h3: One Repair Instead of Yearly Rodding
items.body: Many Naperville homeowners rod their line every year to keep roots out. Lining the damaged section ends that cycle, because the roots no longer have a joint to grow through.

blocks.h2: Signs Your Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: Naperville homeowners usually call us about one of these:

tiles.body: In a busy household, a heater with sediment or a weak burner runs out fast.

tiles.h3: A Puddle in the Utility Room
tiles.body: A valve drip is a repair. Water from the tank body means it's done.
A worn thermocouple or flame sensor, usually a quick fix.
Sediment on the bottom of the tank. A flush may help if it's caught in time.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Naperville Homes
blocks.intro: The median Naperville home was built in 1990. Tank heaters last about 8 to 12 years, so many homes here are on their third heater or more.

items.body: Two-story homes with three or four bathrooms put a lot of demand on one heater. If yours was sized for a smaller household, it may be running past its limit every morning.
DuPage County winters bring nights in the single digits and below. Incoming water is coldest then, and a struggling heater gives out.

items.h3: Utility Rooms Next to Finished Space
items.body: Many heaters here sit in a basement utility room next to finished space. A slow leak can soak carpet before anyone notices.

blocks.h2: Residential Water Heater Service
bodies: We work on every water heater you'll find in a Naperville home: gas and electric tanks, power-vent units, high-efficiency models and tankless heaters. Every visit starts with a diagnosis before any recommendation.

Check the label on the side of the tank for the fuel, the capacity and the manufacture date, and read it to us when you call. Ready for a new one? See [water heater installation](/naperville/water-heater-installation).

blocks.h2: Water Heater Maintenance and Flushing
bodies: A yearly flush clears the sediment that settles at the bottom of every tank, which keeps the heater quieter, faster and longer-lived. We also check the anode rod, the relief valve and the burner or elements.
Most manufacturers recommend flushing about once a year and descaling tankless units regularly. If your heater has never been flushed, a maintenance visit is the right first step.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Naperville Homeowners

items.q: Why does my hot water run out so fast?
items.preview: Usually sediment, a failing part or a heater too small for your household.
items.answer: Usually one of three things: sediment taking up space in the tank, a burner or element that isn't heating fully or a heater that's simply too small for the house. We'll find out which.

items.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
items.preview: A leaking tank means replace. A failed part on a younger heater is usually a repair.
items.answer: If the tank leaks, replace it. If a part failed on a heater under about 8 years old, repair it. If the repair costs a big share of a new heater, we'll tell you.

items.q: How long do water heaters last in Naperville?
items.preview: Tank heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years.
items.answer: Tank heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years, and tankless units often last longer with descaling. Heavy use in a big household can shorten that.

items.q: How often should I flush my water heater?
items.preview: About once a year for a tank. Tankless units need regular descaling.
items.answer: About once a year for a tank heater, and regular descaling for tankless. If your heater has never been flushed, start with a [maintenance visit](#water-heater-maintenance).
